claim: Self-Refine, where a single LLM iteratively generates, critiques, and revises its own output with no additional training/RL, improves outputs by approximately 20% absolute on average across 7 diverse tasks judged by humans and automatic metrics, using GPT-3.5, ChatGPT, and GPT-4.
stance_target: the target paper's claim (ii) that iterative performance feedback degrades LLM-guided proposals
scope_conditions: 7 tasks including dialog response generation and mathematical reasoning; GPT-3.5/ChatGPT/GPT-4 only, no small or quantized models tested
quoted_support: Across all evaluated tasks, outputs generated with Self-Refine are preferred by humans and automatic metrics over those generated with the same LLM using conventional one-step generation, improving by ~20% absolute on average in task performance.

claim: Self-Refine's feedback loop uses the same LLM as generator, critic, and refiner with no external verifier, ground-truth signal, or supervised training data.
stance_target: definition of intrinsic (unverified) self-correction as tested in the mechanism literature
quoted_support: Self-Refine does not require any supervised training data, additional training, or reinforcement learning, and instead uses a single LLM as the generator, refiner, and feedback provider.

claim: Self-Refine demonstrated that even state-of-the-art LLMs like GPT-4 can be further improved at test time via iterative self-feedback, establishing the strongest published positive baseline against which any feedback-degrades-search claim must be positioned.
stance_target: generality of the claim that iterative feedback degrades LLM outputs
scope_conditions: test-time refinement of large frontier models (GPT-4-class), not small/quantized models or combinatorial search tasks with hard external objectives
quoted_support: Our work demonstrates that even state-of-the-art LLMs like GPT-4 can be further improved at test time using our simple, standalone approach.
